subject: Upgrade economics and feature-gating playbook
messages:
From: Laurel Chen <laurel.chen@medbridge.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@medbridge.ai>
Date: Sun, 28 Jun 2026 09:17:00 -0700
Subject: Packaging question — scaling into peak season

Hi Sofia,

Quick question as we finalize our budget for Q4: we expect a 3x surge in inference traffic for two months starting November and want the cleanest path to handle it without a huge step-cost.

Currently on the Compact tier with the Add-on bundle (embeddings, real-time rerank). Options we’re considering: 1) temporary step-up to a higher tier for two months, 2) burst credits / dedicated burst pool, or 3) keep Compact and add dedicated throughput on top.

Key constraints: predictable monthly spend (finance needs a cap), minimal feature regression (we rely on the rerank flow), and contractually we prefer not to re-sign or extend term if we can avoid it. Procurement also asked if there’s any one-time credit or usage smoothing you can offer that doesn’t require a multi-year commit.

Can you sketch the operational and price tradeoffs — and what you’d recommend for a short-duration surge?

Thanks,
Laurel
VP Product, MedBridge AI

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Laurel Chen <laurel.chen@medbridge.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 29 Jun 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Packaging question — scaling into peak season

Laurel — thanks for the clear constraints. I pulled together three pragmatic options (high-level) and attached a pricing matrix that maps expected token volume to estimated spend. Short summary: 

1) Short-term tier upgrade (2-month bump)
   - Pros: simplest operationally, preserves feature parity (no changes to routing or model variants).
   - Cons: full month pricing applies even if usage is lumpy; risk of paying for unused capacity between peaks.

2) Compact + Dedicated Burst Pool
   - Pros: you retain Compact baseline pricing; dedicated burst for the 2-month window priced as a capped committed pool (monthly, cancellable after window). Lower tail cost but a small setup amortization.
   - Cons: slightly more operational coordination (scaling policy and routing rules).

3) Dynamic metered + smoothing credit (no tier change)
   - Pros: no contract changes; we can offer usage smoothing credits and a per-token overage cap so finance has predictability.
   - Cons: higher marginal per-token rate; credits are one-time and amortized against overages — less effective if the surge is extremely large.

Recommendation: Option 2 looks closest to your needs — predictable cap with lower unit cost during the surge and no long-term tier commitment. If Procurement needs a single-line financial instrument, we can do a 2-month burst commitment with a one-time setup credit that offsets the amortization. Jonas — can you confirm burst pool sizing guidance and whether we can formalize a 60-day burst product in a simple amendment?

Next steps: I’ll attach the matrix, and if you approve, I’ll loop Ben (sales lead) to draft the amendment and pricing.

— Sofia
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Hi Laurel — looping in Ben (sales) — oh wait that’s me, hi! ;)

Wanted to add concrete numbers and a discount framing so Procurement can evaluate quickly: based on the forecast you sent, a 2-month dedicated burst pool sized at 3x baseline capacity would cost ~ $42k/month raw. We can structure as:

- 2-month reserved burst pool: $42,000/mo (committed for June–July window)
- One-time setup fee: $3,000 (waived with a 12.5% one-time credit = $375)
- Smoothing credit: we can offer a $5,000 one-time credit applied to overages beyond the committed pool for those two months.

Net impact to your P&L over the 2-month window (after credits) is approx $81k. If you prefer a single invoice line, we can convert to a one-line short-term amendment and include a 6% promo discount (no term extension). That promo requires approval from revenue ops but is within typical concessions for burst windows.

If that math looks reasonable, I’ll draft an amendment and send a short SOW (no change to feature entitlements; routing will be configured by our SRE team).

— Ben
Customer Success & Sales, Redwood Inference

2) A short appendix that confirms the burst pool will not change feature entitlements or data retention settings.
3) An explicit rollback clause: after the two-month window the burst pool will auto-cancel unless MedBridge vs Redwood agree otherwise.

If you can send the amendment and short appendix today, we’ll start internal approvals and try to sign within 48 hours.
